mechanism_narrative: Persistent negative RETAIL_REC over four weeks (-15.1 to -16.0) reflects a structural suppression of discretionary mobility. Without a reversal signal from WORKPLACES or TRANSIT, this suppression persists into the next four weeks, keeping RETAIL_REC negative relative to baseline.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC stable at -15 to -16 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -10 in any of the next four weeks, or WORKPLACES exceeds +5 for two consecutive weeks without RETAIL_REC following within one week.

mechanism_narrative: Rising WORKPLACES mobility (from -3.4 to +2.0 over four weeks) signals return of office commuting. This restores weekday foot traffic patterns and social confidence, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks as commuters resume discretionary shopping.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above 0 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise above -12 within four weeks, or WORKPLACES falls below 0 for two consecutive weeks before RETAIL_REC responds.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has risen steadily (6.4 to 7.7) over four weeks, indicating growing public transport usage. This enables retail access for non-car users. If TRANSIT continues above +7, RETAIL_REC will rise as transport-dependent populations resume shopping trips.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT sustains above +7 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rises from 6.4 to 7.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT falls below +6 in any of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC remains below -14 despite TRANSIT staying above +7.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM remains elevated (+13 to +15) while RETAIL_REC stays suppressed (-15 to -16). This divergence indicates essential-only mobility. If GROCERY_PHARM begins to decline toward baseline while WORKPLACES rises, consumers will reallocate discretionary time to retail, lifting RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below +12 AND WORKPLACES rises above +1 simultaneously
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM remains above +12 for all four weeks, or WORKPLACES falls below 0 before RETAIL_REC rises above -12.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has declined consistently (-11.7 to -13.9) over four weeks, suggesting outdoor recreation is suppressed or weather-constrained. This suppression will persist into the next four weeks, keeping populations indoors and unable to substitute outdoor for retail activity, maintaining RETAIL_REC suppression.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -11 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: PARKS rises above -10 in any of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC rises above -12 despite PARKS staying below -11.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from +8.6 to +5.1 over four weeks, indicating reduced home confinement. Combined with rising TRANSIT (+6.4 to +7.7), this signals policy relaxation. If both trends continue, RETAIL_REC will rise as mobility restrictions ease and populations gain access to retail venues.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below +6 AND TRANSIT rises above +7 in the same week
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rises above +6 for two consecutive weeks, or TRANSIT falls below +6 before RETAIL_REC rises above -12.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has stabilized near +2 over the last two weeks after rising from -3.4. This stabilization at low positive levels indicates partial office return without full commuting restoration. RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed because commuting volumes are insufficient to drive retail foot traffic recovery.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains between 0 and +3 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at +1.9 and +2.0 in last two weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises above +5 in any of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC rises above -12 despite WORKPLACES staying between 0 and +3.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM elevated at +14.1 (t-0w) combined with RETAIL_REC suppressed at -15.1 indicates consumers are consolidating trips to essential venues only. If GROCERY_PHARM falls below +10 over the next week while PARKS remains below -12, consumers will shift discretionary spending to retail as essential-trip consolidation ends and outdoor substitutes remain unavailable.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below +10 in week t+1 AND PARKS remains below -12
regime_hint: transition from essential-only to discretionary mobility
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM remains above +12 for all four weeks, or PARKS rises above -10 before RETAIL_REC rises above -12.
